correctness.rationale: For a strictly positive continuous real planar gauge, every maximizer on the convexified unit ball lies on a supporting segment with endpoints in the original unit ball; hence the sharp two-summand coefficient equals the maximum gauge on the convexification. In the eight-ray fan, the original unit ball is a union of eight radial triangles, so its convex hull is the hull of the eight nodal radial unit vertices. Conewise linearity reduces maxima to hull vertices or edge-ray crossings; every possible strict crossing among all unordered pairs reduces by antipodal symmetry to the twelve distinct values tabulated in the proof. Conversely each chord-ray crossing is a convex combination of two original unit vertices and supplies an extremizer. The twelve rational witness quadruples each strictly dominate all eleven competitors and one. An independent pure-Python exact rational hull computation passed 4096 octagonal tuples, 12 irredundancy witnesses and 1728 hexagonal controls; these are supplemental rather than infinite proofs.

Indexed regular-octagon Banach-space results and planar convexification results concern different invariants. value.rationale: The best quasi-triangle coefficient is the operational stability constant of any quasi-norm and is directly relevant to nonconvex regularization and numerical estimates. The result completely classifies this natural four-parameter octagonal fan for all positive real weights and proves that twelve distinct competing chord configurations are all necessary, rather than merely giving a finite numerical value. It supplies an explicit computable coefficient and exact extremizing directions beyond the source paper’s M/m estimate. The classification is not a textbook consequence of convexity since the gauges are generally nonconvex and the case analysis has twelve irredundant regimes. No downstream theorem or arbitrary-dimensional generalization is claimed.
